chapter: Lake boats and brass band practice
title: Reading brass bands, hunky-tunk bands and band size
summary: George says old funeral and parade bands were reading bands, describes 'tunk bands' at the back, and gives a size of ten to twelve pieces.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: George, you said you think they, they had the bands even a long time ago in the funeral center?
Yeah. Oh yeah, sure they did.
Well did they play a ear when you were a child?
No, most of them were reading bands.
Most of those brass bands were reading.

Well they had a few get together bands, they like, the Labor Day, they have so many bands that they had to send out to countries and get them, you know. Well they'd have a few get together bands that were playing this, the hit stuff like that.
So would they get real ratty in the street? Oh yeah, sure.
They used to call them a tunk band, they'd put them way in the back. What'd they call them? Tunk bands.

You know like hunky tunk. Hunky tunk bands, yeah. Well I wanted to ask too while I met it, Abby played a parade two weeks ago and he was saying over those days, several years ago when you had your little six piece band or something like that, a brass band, you got a lot of more jobs on the street and it sounded good and all too. Did you only use about six or seven pieces in the street at one time or not? No. Abby was talking like you said then the union makes them use ten now.
But how big a band when you did have one a few years ago with your name on that drummer, just, we always see that.
Nothing under ten. Nothing under ten. You don't think it was under ten? No.
Ten to twelve, from eleven to twelve the most.
Well how big were the bands when you were a child?

Did you ever count? I never noticed no more than twelve. I never noticed no more than twelve. So times haven't changed too much? No it hasn't changed in that line at all. More than the only change that you find that the bands are not reading, because they had really good brass bands at the time. Because most of them guys that played those few marches weren't no men that played dances, they were just, men you know they played baritone, you don't find no baritone, you don't find no mellophone. No.
